rationale: The two solutions use the same algorithm and structure: try every start stone in both orientations, then backtrack and place stones in either orientation. The only material difference is naming. A calls the placed-count parameter `length`. B calls it `l`, which is easy to confuse with the digit 1 and which Go style generally discourages, and B adds a longer comment to make up for the opaque name. Both share the same minor inefficiency (they retry the same start stone and duplicate the place/undo blocks). A's clearer naming makes it marginally better.
